current_episode.title: Catching Up On Climate 2026 Episode 1 | Dirk Forrister, President & CEO, International Emissions Trading Association (IETA)

guest.bio_context: Dirk Forrister has served as President and CEO of IETA for 14 years and is stepping down from this role while remaining involved as a senior advisor. He has been instrumental in advocating for carbon market provisions in international climate agreements, including the Paris Agreement, and has led research projects with Harvard and other institutions on carbon pricing and market design.

pending_qa.q: Why are serious, legally-binding climate targets with flexibility mechanisms essential compared to aspirational targets?
pending_qa.r: Forrister argues that the past approach of picking arbitrary numbers and accepting failure is no longer viable. The goal is to have serious targets that people will stick to, embedded in law, that allow flexibilities so companies can really achieve the objectives of the Paris Agreement. As reality sets in about how tough targets are, businesses recognize that flexibility through market approaches enables them to manage their own trajectories and find efficiencies for lowering costs while still meeting mandatory compliance.

pending_qa.q: What role did IETA play in securing carbon market provisions in the Paris Agreement?
pending_qa.r: IETA submitted a proposal for carbon market language in response to UN Secretary General Ban Ki-moon's call for industry input. Working with WBCSD and corporate leaders group, they developed economic modeling showing potential cost savings and emission reductions. They collaborated with Harvard and international modelers at the University of Maryland on research about what should be included. During final negotiations, IETA urged delegations to reconsider when the provision nearly failed, working with environmental partners to secure what became a full article on carbon markets—the very last item agreed in the Paris Agreement.
